rows.evidence: capabilities_test.exs:100 — `refute Map.has_key?(decoded, "elicitation")`. This addresses the check's PRECONDITION (`d&&e in d`), not its axis: it asserts the branch on which the check SKIPS. A precondition is not an axis and a claim about one is neither agreement nor contradiction.

rows.the_near_miss_that_is_not_a_counterpart: `ClientDeclaresElicitationCapability`. Its one axis, `capability_value_is_a_plain_object`, is a predicate on a DECLARED capability's value; the case this claim asserts, an undeclared one being absent, is the check's PRECONDITION (`d&&e in d`, the branch on which it skips), and a precondition is not an axis. So the claim shares the check's subject and touches none of its predicate: no match under rule A. A sweep for `omit`/`absent`/`missing` alone returns the SEP-2243 header rows (`ClientCustomHeaderOmitNull`, the `Missing Mcp-Method header` rows). They are about headers, not capabilities, and the pattern keeps the two words together for that reason.

rows.owner: MES-133 (D1) — rule B (A3 §6, MES-110; PO 2026-09-24). Before MES-110: unowned, and unownable by this suite — CONFIRMED from INSIDE the declared population rather than argued from outside it: C1c-iv-a declares all eight `caching` checks and decomposed every one of them, and not one axis reads what the server was configured with.
rows.placement_and_why: A structured `claims_without_an_edge` row, which is the W-4 shape and not the edge-prose one. Chosen because the residual is a WHOLE CLAIM of the member rather than a sharper reading of a claim that already has an edge: `ttlMs` 0 and `cacheScope` `public` are edges, and `and these are the DEFAULTS` is a third thing the member asserts and nothing scores. Until MES-110 the file had no criterion that would make this choice forced rather than argued — see the note on the `:237/:238` edge. Since MES-110, rule B (A3 §6) says what this row IS: an `oc:none` token on an edge-bearing member is a claim-level unmatched record. It does not say that an uncovered sub-claim must take this form rather than edge prose; that is MES-133's (D1) question.
rows.the_near_miss_that_is_not_a_counterpart: `DefaultResultTypeComplete` — and it is the only row in all 175 that matches `(?i)\bdefault|\bconfigur`, so a reader greping for `default` finds exactly one hit and could stop at it. It is not a counterpart on three counts: it is CLIENT leg, its subject is `resultType` rather than any caching field, and its `default` is a SPEC default — how a client must read an ABSENT field — not a deployment's unconfigured state. The nearer rows by subject are this file's own five `*CachingHints` plus `TtlNonNegative` and `CacheScopeValid`, which this member DOES carry edges onto; they score the values and are silent on where the values came from.
rows.the_search_as_first_recorded: an OC check that establishes what a server does when a policy is NOT configured — a DEFAULT as distinct from a setting — by varying the implementation's configuration between runs or by reading it, rather than scoring whatever values the single server under test happened to return
rows.the_search_that_found_none: what a server's caching hints are when NO caching policy is configured: the DEFAULT values, as distinct from a setting
rows.why_it_is_recorded_here_and_not_in_bucke: The member is EDGE-BEARING — its two value assertions carry four edges between them — and a bucket-1 row is a statement about a MEMBER with no counterpart at all. Until MES-110, A3 §6's state 3 was read as a property of a member, so a sub-claim of an edge-bearing member had no bucket and was escalated instead. Since MES-110 state 3 is read per token (rule B, A3 §6): this sub-claim is a claim-level unmatched record in the `claim-unmatched` view, owned by MES-133 (D1), and it is not escalated. The placement among the three the file uses for such residuals is argued in `placement_and_why`.
rows.why_no_axis_reaches_it: Every caching axis is a predicate on a result the harness received from ONE server in ONE configuration; nothing in the suite varies a server's configuration or asks what it was, so no OC check can distinguish a value that was configured from one that was not. The distinction is the whole point of this member — it is the regression guard on the no-store default — and it is invisible to the harness in principle rather than by omission.

title: claim-unmatched — claims with no counterpart inside edge-bearing members, in NO bucket
what_this_is: THE TWELFTH VIEW, OUTSIDE THE TEN AND IN NO EQUATION. A3 §6 as amended by rule B (MES-110; PO 2026-09-24) makes an `oc:none` token on an edge-bearing member a claim-level unmatched record: bucket 1 at the grain of one claim. The ten buckets count members, checks or edges, and adding claims to any of them would put two units in one count, so these are listed here with their own count. Every row's member carries an edge, which [claim_unmatched] checks; the rows are the crosswalk's own records, so a reader can check this view against the matrix byte for byte.
